}}

{{recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Squid|squid]] tubes and tentacles
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], beaten
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] iced [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|Cornmeal]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 3 tbsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Quart|quarts]] [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut]] or [[Cookbook:Safflower Oil|safflower oil]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
== Procedure ==
#Rinse the squid thoroughly and pat dry. Cut the tentacles in half lengthwise and the tubes into ½-inch rings. Set aside.
#Combine parsley, garlic, salt, pepper, eggs, flour, and lemon juice. Transfer to large bowl.
#[[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] squid pieces in cornmeal, then wet mixture, then again in cornmeal. Set aside.
#Heat oil in a deep-fryer or cast-iron [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]] to 400°F. Add squid, 4 at a time, and [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep fry]] for 45 seconds to a minute. Drain on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]] and repeat with remaining squid.
#Sprinkle calamari with some more kosher salt and freshly-ground black pepper, and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* A lot of recipes for calamari call to marinate the squid in an acidic liquid to tenderize them. However, this wouldn't work even if you let it sit for years. See, marinades only penetrate about, at most, ¼ inch. That isn't far enough to get to the tough connective tissues deep in the center. So throw away all those recipes that call to "tenderize" with acid, and just cook squid either very, very fast, or very, very long.
